questionText: Which of the following BEST describes e-procurement?
options: The manual process of issuing purchase orders through paper-based systems
The use of internet-based technology to automate and streamline the procurement process from requisition to payment
The process of procuring goods exclusively from local suppliers
The use of telephone communication to negotiate with suppliers

questionText: Which technology is MOST commonly used to automate supplier catalog management in e-procurement systems?
options: Fax machines
Electronic catalog (e-catalog) integrated into a procurement portal
Manual spreadsheet tracking
Physical supplier brochures stored in filing cabinets

questionText: An organization wants to reduce procurement cycle time and paper usage. Which technology adoption would MOST directly achieve both goals?
options: Hiring more procurement staff
Implementing an e-procurement system with automated purchase order generation and electronic approval workflows
Increasing the frequency of supplier meetings
Printing purchase orders in batches at the end of each month

questionText: Which of the following technologies enables buyers to compare supplier prices in real time during the procurement process?
options: Manual telephone quotations
Online reverse auctions and e-sourcing platforms
Printed supplier catalogs
Fax-based quotation requests

questionText: RFID technology in procurement operations is MOST useful for:
options: Drafting supplier contracts
Automatically identifying and tracking incoming goods at the receiving dock without manual scanning
Processing supplier invoices electronically
Sending purchase orders to suppliers

questionText: Which of the following is a PRIMARY advantage of using e-procurement technology over traditional procurement methods?
options: It eliminates the need for supplier relationships entirely
It reduces procurement costs, improves transparency, speeds up the procurement cycle, and provides better data for decision-making
It guarantees the lowest prices from all suppliers
It removes all human involvement from the procurement process

questionText: A company wants to automate the matching of purchase orders, goods received notes, and supplier invoices. Which technology BEST supports this "three-way matching" process?
options: Manual audit by the finance department
An integrated e-procurement or ERP system with automated three-way matching functionality
Scanning paper invoices into image files
Emailing invoices to the accounts payable team

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes a "procurement portal" in e-procurement?
options: A physical office where suppliers submit bids
A web-based platform where buyers can browse supplier catalogs, place orders, and manage procurement transactions electronically
A government office that regulates procurement activities
A manual filing system for procurement documents

questionText: In e-procurement, "spend analysis" technology helps organizations to:
options: Monitor employee attendance in the procurement department
Analyze procurement expenditure data to identify savings opportunities, compliance gaps, and supplier consolidation possibilities
Calculate the total number of purchase orders issued annually
Measure the speed of the procurement team

questionText: Which technology enables suppliers to submit bids electronically in a structured format during a competitive tendering process?
options: Paper-based tender box submission
Electronic tendering (e-tendering) platform
Fax-based bid submission system
Manual bid collection by procurement officers

questionText: A manufacturing company wants to give employees a simple way to order pre-approved office supplies from preferred suppliers without going through the full procurement process. Which e-procurement tool is MOST appropriate?
options: A full strategic sourcing platform
A self-service e-catalog with a shopping cart interface limited to pre-approved items and suppliers
A government procurement portal
A manual requisition form submitted to the procurement department

questionText: Which of the following is a key challenge in implementing e-procurement technology in organizations in developing countries like Ethiopia?
options: Excess availability of high-speed internet in all regions
Limited internet infrastructure, low digital literacy among suppliers, resistance to change, and integration challenges with existing systems
Over-abundance of qualified e-procurement technology vendors
Too many suppliers already using e-procurement platforms

questionText: E-auctions in procurement differ from traditional tendering primarily because:
options: E-auctions require more paperwork than traditional tendering
E-auctions allow suppliers to submit and revise bids in real time during a defined auction event, often resulting in more competitive pricing
E-auctions can only be used for service contracts
E-auctions eliminate the need for supplier qualification

questionText: Which of the following technologies supports automated supplier performance monitoring in e-procurement?
options: Paper-based supplier scorecards updated annually
Supplier management modules within e-procurement systems that track delivery, quality, and compliance metrics in real time
Telephone-based supplier feedback collection
Manual spreadsheet tracking updated by procurement staff monthly

questionText: In e-procurement, "contract management technology" primarily helps organizations to:
options: Design new products for procurement
Store, manage, monitor, and ensure compliance with supplier contracts electronically, including tracking key dates and obligations
Process employee payroll linked to procurement activities
Design the layout of procurement offices

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes a Business-to-Business (B2B) e-commerce model?
options: Individual consumers purchasing products directly from an online retailer
Commercial transactions conducted electronically between businesses, such as a manufacturer ordering components from a supplier through an online platform
Government agencies purchasing goods from private companies online
Consumers selling second-hand goods to other consumers online

questionText: A Business-to-Consumer (B2C) e-commerce model is characterized by:
options: Transactions between two or more businesses conducted online
Businesses selling products or services directly to individual end consumers through online platforms
Consumers selling products to government entities online
Governments providing services to citizens through online portals

questionText: Which e-commerce business model is illustrated when a company like Alibaba connects buyers and sellers without holding inventory itself?
options: Business-to-Consumer (B2C)
Marketplace or platform model, often classified as B2B or C2C depending on the participants
Consumer-to-Business (C2B)
Government-to-Business (G2B)

questionText: A Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C) e-commerce model is BEST illustrated by:
options: A retailer selling products to customers through its website
An online platform such as eBay where individual consumers buy and sell products to each other
A government procurement portal for public tenders
A business purchasing raw materials from a supplier online

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the "drop-shipping" e-commerce fulfillment model?
options: A retailer that manufactures its own products and ships them directly from its factory
A retailer that takes customer orders and transfers them to a supplier or manufacturer who ships directly to the customer, without the retailer holding inventory
A logistics company that drops shipments at a central warehouse for later distribution
A consumer who ships goods purchased online back to the seller

questionText: In e-commerce supply chain management, the MAIN challenge of a direct-to-consumer (D2C) model compared to selling through traditional retail channels is:
options: Higher product manufacturing costs
Managing high volumes of small individual orders, last-mile delivery complexity, returns management, and customer service at scale
Difficulty in setting product prices online
Lack of access to customer data

questionText: Which e-commerce business model allows individual professionals to offer services to businesses online, such as freelance logistics consulting?
options: B2B
Consumer-to-Business (C2B)
B2C
G2C

questionText: A Government-to-Business (G2B) e-commerce model in procurement refers to:
options: Businesses selling products to individual government employees online
Government entities using electronic platforms to conduct procurement, licensing, and regulatory transactions with businesses
Businesses providing technology services to governments
Government employees purchasing personal items online

questionText: Which of the following is the MOST significant supply chain implication of the growth of B2C e-commerce?
options: Reduced demand for transportation services
Increased need for last-mile delivery capabilities, flexible fulfillment networks, efficient returns processing, and real-time order visibility
Decreased importance of warehouse management systems
Simplified inventory management due to lower order frequency

questionText: A company uses a "subscription box" e-commerce model. What is the PRIMARY supply chain advantage of this model?
options: It eliminates the need for demand forecasting entirely
It provides predictable, recurring demand that simplifies supply chain planning, inventory management, and fulfillment scheduling
It allows the company to sell products at higher prices than traditional retail
It eliminates the need for packaging and labeling

questionText: Which e-commerce business model is MOST relevant to public procurement in Ethiopia under the new procurement regulations?
options: C2C marketplace model
G2B e-procurement model where government entities use electronic platforms to solicit bids, award contracts, and manage supplier relationships
B2C subscription model
C2B freelance service model

questionText: An online marketplace that charges sellers a commission on each transaction while providing the platform infrastructure is using which revenue model?
options: Subscription-based revenue model
Commission-based or transaction fee revenue model
Advertising-only revenue model
Freemium revenue model

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the "freemium" e-commerce business model?
options: Offering all products for free to all customers
Providing a basic version of a product or service for free while charging for premium features or enhanced functionality
Charging a flat monthly subscription for unlimited access to all products
Offering free shipping on all orders regardless of order value

questionText: How does the "platform economy" model differ from traditional supply chain models in e-commerce?
options: Platform models require more physical infrastructure than traditional models
Platform models connect buyers and sellers digitally without owning the goods, creating value through network effects rather than traditional production and distribution
Platform models rely entirely on physical retail stores for transactions
Platform models are only applicable to government procurement

questionText: A logistics company decides to offer an online freight marketplace connecting shippers with carriers. This is an example of which e-commerce model applied to supply chain?
options: B2C product retail
B2B digital freight marketplace enabling supply chain transactions between logistics buyers and service providers
C2C consumer resale platform
G2B government procurement portal

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes "omnichannel" supply chain strategy in e-commerce?
options: Using only online sales channels and eliminating all physical stores

Integrating all sales channels — online, mobile, and physical — so that customers experience seamless service and supply chain operations support all channels from a unified inventory and fulfillment system
Selling products through a single online platform exclusively
Using multiple suppliers for each product category regardless of channel

questionText: A company sells customized products through its website where customers design their own items before ordering. This is an example of which e-commerce and supply chain integration concept?
options: Make-to-stock with online ordering
Mass customization enabled by e-commerce, where customer-configured orders trigger a make-to-order or assemble-to-order supply chain process
Batch production sold through an online catalog
Reverse logistics managed through an e-commerce platform

questionText: Which e-commerce business model creates the GREATEST demand for dynamic, real-time supply chain visibility?
options: Physical retail with manual inventory management
Online marketplaces and D2C e-commerce where customers expect real-time order tracking from purchase to delivery
Wholesale distribution through traditional intermediaries
Government tenders managed through paper-based systems

questionText: In comparing B2B and B2C e-commerce supply chain requirements, which statement is MOST accurate?
options: B2C e-commerce typically involves larger order quantities and fewer, more predictable orders than B2B
B2B e-commerce typically involves larger, more predictable orders with negotiated terms, while B2C involves high volumes of small, variable orders requiring fast, flexible fulfillment
Both B2B and B2C e-commerce have identical supply chain requirements
B2C supply chains are always simpler than B2B supply chains

questionText: A company in Ethiopia is deciding whether to enter the e-commerce market. Which factor represents the GREATEST opportunity for e-commerce growth in Ethiopia?
options: An oversupply of traditional retail stores making online competition difficult
Growing mobile internet penetration, increasing smartphone adoption, a young population, and the government's digital economy agenda creating an expanding online consumer base
A fully developed payment infrastructure already supporting all forms of online payment
An excess of logistics providers specializing in last-mile e-commerce delivery

questionText: E-procurement is BEST described as:
options: A manual paper-based system for managing supplier relationships
The use of electronic systems and the internet to conduct procurement processes including sourcing, ordering, and payment
The outsourcing of all procurement activities to a third-party provider
A government regulation requiring all companies to procure goods locally

questionText: Which of the following is NOT a recognized type of e-procurement?
options: E-sourcing
E-tendering
E-payment
E-storage

questionText: "E-sourcing" in procurement refers to:
options: Paying suppliers electronically after delivery
Using internet-based tools to identify, evaluate, and select suppliers, including activities such as e-RFI, e-RFP, and e-auctions
Managing supplier contracts in a digital document management system
Tracking the movement of goods using electronic sensors

questionText: A "Request for Quotation (RFQ)" submitted electronically to multiple suppliers simultaneously is an example of which e-procurement activity?
options: E-payment
E-sourcing through electronic request for quotation
E-invoicing
E-cataloging

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes "e-ordering" in the context of e-procurement?
options: Placing orders verbally with suppliers over the telephone
Generating, approving, and transmitting purchase orders to suppliers electronically through an automated system
Manually typing purchase orders and emailing them as attachments
Collecting supplier invoices and filing them electronically

questionText: What is the PRIMARY benefit of "e-invoicing" in supply chain procurement operations?
options: It increases the number of suppliers in the procurement network
It automates invoice processing, reduces errors, speeds up payment cycles, and improves cash flow visibility for both buyers and suppliers
It eliminates the need for supplier contracts
It replaces the need for a procurement department

questionText: "Maverick spending" in procurement refers to:
options: Innovative procurement strategies that achieve cost savings
Purchasing outside approved procurement processes or preferred supplier contracts, leading to compliance failures and cost inefficiencies
Procurement of luxury or non-essential items
Emergency procurement conducted outside normal timelines

questionText: E-procurement systems help reduce "maverick spending" primarily by:
options: Restricting employees from making any purchasing decisions
Channeling employee purchases through approved e-catalogs and automated approval workflows that enforce compliance with procurement policies
Eliminating all discretionary spending across the organization
Requiring all purchases to be approved by the CEO

questionText: Which of the following is a key distinction between "direct" and "indirect" procurement in e-procurement?
options: Direct procurement refers to all purchases made directly from manufacturers, while indirect procurement refers to purchases through intermediaries

Direct procurement involves goods that go directly into the product being manufactured (e.g., raw materials), while indirect procurement covers goods and services that support operations but are not part of the end product (e.g., office supplies, IT services)
Direct procurement is always conducted electronically, while indirect procurement uses paper-based processes
Direct procurement is only applicable to government organizations

questionText: In e-procurement, a "preferred supplier list" is used to:
options: Identify suppliers who have offered the lowest prices in the past
Maintain a pre-qualified roster of approved suppliers that have been evaluated for quality, reliability, and compliance, streamlining future procurement decisions
List all suppliers who have ever submitted a bid to the organization
Record suppliers who have been blacklisted due to poor performance

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the concept of "e-procurement integration" with an ERP system?
options: Installing e-procurement software on the same server as the ERP
Connecting the e-procurement platform with the ERP system so that procurement transactions automatically update financial, inventory, and supplier data without manual re-entry
Using the ERP system to replace the e-procurement platform entirely
Printing ERP reports for use in the procurement department

questionText: A company implements an e-procurement system and notices that procurement cycle time has decreased by 60%. This improvement is MOST likely due to:
options: Hiring more experienced procurement staff
Automated workflows, electronic approvals, and real-time supplier communication replacing manual, paper-based processes that previously caused delays
Reducing the number of suppliers in the network
Increasing the budget allocated to the procurement department

questionText: Which of the following is a LIMITATION of e-procurement implementation?
options: E-procurement always increases procurement costs significantly
Implementation challenges including high initial technology investment, resistance from staff and suppliers, data security risks, and the need for process redesign and training
E-procurement prevents organizations from using multiple suppliers
E-procurement eliminates all forms of contract management

questionText: "Dynamic pricing" in e-procurement means:
options: Setting fixed prices for all products in the e-catalog
Prices that change in real time based on supply and demand conditions, market fluctuations, or competitive bidding dynamics
Pricing strategies determined exclusively by government regulations
Offering discounts to suppliers who deliver on time

questionText: Which of the following e-procurement models allows buyers to aggregate demand across multiple organizations to achieve volume discounts?
options: Individual spot purchasing
Consortium buying or group purchasing through a shared e-procurement platform
Single-source procurement without competitive bidding
Emergency procurement outside normal processes

questionText: In e-procurement, "total cost of ownership" analysis is supported by technology through:
options: Simply comparing supplier unit prices electronically
Aggregating and analyzing all cost data including purchase price, delivery, quality, and lifecycle costs from integrated procurement and ERP systems to inform more complete sourcing decisions
Asking suppliers to submit their own total cost calculations
Using spreadsheets to manually add up all procurement costs

questionText: An organization's procurement team uses an e-procurement system to conduct supplier sustainability assessments. This practice BEST represents:
options: Using technology only for financial procurement decisions
Integrating sustainability criteria into the e-procurement workflow to evaluate and monitor supplier environmental and social performance alongside traditional procurement metrics
Restricting procurement to local suppliers only
Outsourcing sustainability assessments to a government body

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes "punch-out catalogs" in e-procurement?
options: Physical supplier catalogs that buyers punch holes in for filing

Hosted supplier catalogs that are accessed from within the buyer's e-procurement system, allowing buyers to shop on the supplier's website while maintaining integration with the buyer's approval and ordering workflows
Catalogs used exclusively for government procurement
Outdated catalogs removed from the e-procurement system

questionText: In e-procurement, "supplier onboarding" refers to:
options: Training procurement staff on new software
The process of registering, verifying, and integrating new suppliers into the organization's e-procurement system, including documentation, qualification, and system setup
Transporting new suppliers to the buyer's facility for a site visit
Issuing the first purchase order to a new supplier

questionText: A procurement manager observes that the organization's e-procurement adoption rate among suppliers is low. Which intervention is MOST likely to improve adoption?
options: Mandating all suppliers to adopt the system immediately under threat of contract termination
Providing supplier training, technical support, simplified onboarding processes, and clearly communicating the mutual benefits of e-procurement adoption
Reducing the number of preferred suppliers to those already using the system
Switching to a paper-based backup system for non-adopting suppliers

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes an "e-payment system" in the context of supply chain and e-commerce?
options: A physical cash payment made at a supplier's office
An electronic method of transferring funds between buyers and sellers to settle commercial transactions, including bank transfers, digital wallets, and payment gateways
A manual cheque-writing process managed by the finance department
A barter exchange system conducted online

questionText: Which of the following is an example of a "digital wallet" used in e-commerce transactions?
options: A physical leather wallet used to carry cash
A mobile or online application such as PayPal, Apple Pay, or telebirr that stores payment information and enables electronic transactions
A bank account accessed through a physical branch
A prepaid debit card purchased at a retail store

questionText: In supply chain e-payment systems, "Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT)" is BEST described as:
options: Physically transporting cash between a buyer and supplier
The electronic transfer of money from one bank account to another, used to pay suppliers directly without paper cheques
Scanning paper cheques and emailing them to suppliers
A mobile payment system used exclusively for retail consumer purchases

questionText: Which payment method is MOST commonly associated with international supply chain transactions involving large payment amounts between businesses?
options: Cash on delivery
Letters of credit or bank wire transfers (SWIFT), which provide security and assurance for both buyer and supplier in cross-border trade
Mobile money transfers
Digital gift cards

questionText: A "payment gateway" in e-commerce refers to:
options: A physical point-of-sale terminal at a retail store
A technology service that authorizes and processes online payment transactions between buyers and sellers, connecting e-commerce platforms with banks and payment networks
A government office that approves all online payments
A manual approval process for large procurement payments

questionText: Which of the following e-payment challenges is MOST significant for e-commerce in Ethiopia?
options: Excessive availability of payment options making selection difficult
Limited penetration of formal banking services, low credit card ownership, and nascent digital payment infrastructure, though mobile money platforms like telebirr are expanding access
Oversupply of payment gateways competing for market share
Too many international payment providers operating in the market

questionText: In e-commerce supply chain transactions, "escrow payment" services are used to:
options: Delay all payments indefinitely until a dispute arises
Hold buyer payment securely until the buyer confirms satisfactory receipt of goods, reducing risk for both parties in online transactions
Transfer funds directly to the seller before goods are shipped
Process payments exclusively in foreign currencies

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes "mobile payment" systems and their relevance to supply chain e-commerce in Africa?
options: Mobile payments are irrelevant to supply chain transactions in Africa

Mobile payment platforms such as M-Pesa in Kenya and telebirr in Ethiopia are enabling digital commerce and supply chain transactions in markets where traditional banking and card payment infrastructure is limited
Mobile payments are only useful for consumer retail transactions, not supply chain operations
Mobile payments require a full banking license to operate in all African countries

questionText: "Cryptocurrency" as a payment method in international supply chain transactions offers which potential advantage?
options: It is regulated and guaranteed by all central banks globally
It can facilitate cross-border payments without traditional banking intermediaries, potentially reducing transaction costs and settlement times, though it carries high volatility and regulatory risks
It eliminates all risks associated with international payments
It is widely accepted by all suppliers globally as a standard payment method

questionText: Which of the following is a key security feature of modern e-payment systems used in supply chain transactions?
options: Requiring all payments to be made in person at a bank branch
Encryption of payment data, multi-factor authentication, tokenization of card data, and fraud detection algorithms that protect transactions from unauthorized access
Using paper receipts as the sole verification of payment
Limiting all transactions to amounts below a fixed threshold

questionText: "Straight-through processing (STP)" in supply chain e-payments refers to:
options: Processing payments only in a straight line from buyer to seller without any intermediaries
Automated end-to-end processing of payment transactions without manual intervention, from invoice receipt through payment authorization to fund transfer and reconciliation
Restricting payments to a single approved payment method
Processing only payments that have been manually approved by senior management

questionText: A company wants to improve supplier payment terms to strengthen supplier relationships. Which e-payment technology best supports offering suppliers early payment discounts (dynamic discounting)?
options: Paper-based payment processing
A supply chain finance platform that allows buyers to offer early payment to suppliers at a discount, improving supplier cash flow while earning a return for the buyer
Extending payment terms from 30 to 90 days
Paying all suppliers on the same fixed date regardless of invoice date

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes "e-invoicing" and its link to e-payment in supply chain management?
options: Printing invoices and delivering them physically to the accounts payable department

The electronic generation, transmission, and processing of invoices, which when integrated with e-payment systems enables automated invoice matching, approval, and payment, significantly reducing the order-to-cash and procure-to-pay cycle times
Scanning paper invoices into PDF files and emailing them to buyers
Using phone calls to confirm invoice amounts before manual payment

questionText: Which regulatory consideration is MOST important when implementing e-payment systems for cross-border supply chain transactions involving Ethiopia?
options: The font size used on electronic payment receipts
National Bank of Ethiopia foreign exchange regulations, anti-money laundering requirements, and international payment compliance standards that govern cross-border fund transfers
The color scheme of the e-payment platform interface
The physical location of the payment processing server

questionText: A logistics company wants to implement a real-time payment system for freight services. Which e-payment feature is MOST critical for this use case?
options: Delayed batch payment processing at the end of each month
Real-time payment confirmation and reconciliation integrated with the transportation management system to automatically trigger payment upon delivery confirmation
Cash payment collected by the driver at delivery
Monthly paper-based invoicing to customers

questionText: A Supply Chain Information System (SCIS) is BEST described as:
options: A manual filing system for supply chain documents
An integrated set of technology tools and platforms that collect, process, store, and distribute supply chain data to support planning, execution, and decision-making across the supply chain
A government database of registered logistics companies
A software system used exclusively for warehouse management

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the role of an ERP system in supply chain information management?
options: Managing only the financial accounting functions of the organization
Integrating data across business functions including procurement, production, inventory, logistics, and finance into a single unified database, enabling coordinated supply chain decision-making
Replacing all supply chain managers with automated decision-making
Managing only customer-facing sales and marketing activities

questionText: "Data integration" in supply chain information systems refers to:
options: Printing data from multiple systems and manually combining them into a single report
The seamless consolidation of data from disparate systems across the supply chain into a unified view that enables consistent, accurate information sharing and decision-making
Using a single spreadsheet to track all supply chain data
Restricting data access to only senior management

questionText: A supply chain manager receives conflicting inventory data from the warehouse management system and the ERP system. The ROOT CAUSE of this discrepancy is MOST likely:
options: The warehouse is too large to manage effectively
Poor data integration between systems, data entry errors, or lack of real-time synchronization between the WMS and ERP platforms
The supply chain manager is not checking the right system
Inventory levels are too high to be tracked accurately

questionText: Which of the following information flows is MOST critical for effective supply chain planning?
options: Marketing campaign performance data
Demand forecasts, inventory levels, order status, supplier lead times, and production schedules shared in real time across supply chain partners
Employee performance reviews from the HR department
Financial audit reports from the external auditor

questionText: "Supply chain visibility" enabled by information systems means:
options: Installing cameras in all warehouses for physical monitoring
Having real-time access to accurate information about the status of inventory, orders, shipments, and supply chain events across all nodes and partners in the supply chain
Publishing supply chain data in annual reports
Monitoring only the final stage of delivery to the customer

questionText: Which of the following technologies provides real-time data on the location and condition of goods in transit for supply chain information systems?
options: Monthly delivery status reports submitted by carriers
GPS tracking, IoT sensors, and telematics systems integrated with the supply chain management platform
Phone calls from drivers reporting their location
Paper-based delivery manifests submitted after delivery

questionText: A "supply chain control tower" powered by an information system enables:
options: Physical monitoring of warehouse security
End-to-end supply chain visibility, event monitoring, exception alerting, and decision support by consolidating data from multiple supply chain systems into a single real-time dashboard
Automated production of all supply chain goods
Complete elimination of human decision-making in the supply chain

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes "master data management" in supply chain information systems?
options: Managing the physical master copies of procurement contracts
The discipline of ensuring that critical supply chain data — such as supplier information, product details, and customer records — is accurate, consistent, and maintained across all systems
Training managers to use supply chain software
Backing up supply chain data to an external hard drive

questionText: In supply chain information systems, "application programming interfaces" (APIs) are used to:
options: Train supply chain staff on using new software
Enable different software systems to communicate and exchange data automatically, facilitating integration between e-commerce platforms, ERP systems, WMS, TMS, and other supply chain tools
Design the user interface of supply chain software
Process financial transactions between buyers and suppliers

questionText: A company's supply chain information system generates demand forecasts but the accuracy is consistently low. Which intervention would MOST improve forecast accuracy?
options: Increasing safety stock to compensate for forecast errors

Incorporating additional data inputs such as point-of-sale data, market intelligence, and machine learning algorithms into the forecasting model, and regularly reviewing and adjusting forecast parameters
Reducing the frequency of demand forecast updates
Switching to a manual forecasting process

questionText: "Event-driven supply chain management" supported by information systems means:
options: Managing supply chain events only during annual planning cycles
Using real-time alerts and automated responses triggered by supply chain events — such as a delayed shipment or a supplier quality failure — to enable rapid corrective action
Scheduling supply chain activities only around major corporate events
Reacting to supply chain disruptions only after they have been fully resolved

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the supply chain information flow in a "demand-driven" supply chain?
options: Information flows from manufacturers to retailers to consumers

Actual customer demand signals (e.g., point-of-sale data) flow upstream from retailers through the supply chain, triggering replenishment and production decisions based on real demand rather than forecasts
Demand information flows only between the company and its tier-1 suppliers
Demand information is collected annually through customer surveys

questionText: A cloud-based supply chain information platform offers which PRIMARY advantage over on-premise systems for multi-partner supply chains?
options: Greater control over physical server hardware
Easier and faster data sharing across multiple supply chain partners regardless of geographic location, with lower upfront investment and scalable capacity
Higher data security due to local storage
Reduced need for internet connectivity

questionText: In supply chain information systems, "analytics maturity" progresses from:
options: Real-time analytics directly to descriptive analytics
Descriptive analytics (what happened) to diagnostic analytics (why it happened) to predictive analytics (what will happen) to prescriptive analytics (what should be done)
Predictive analytics to descriptive analytics in reverse order
Manual reporting to physical observation to digital tracking

questionText: In the context of supply chain e-commerce, "cybersecurity" refers to:
options: The physical security of warehouses and distribution centers
The protection of computer systems, networks, data, and digital supply chain assets from unauthorized access, cyberattacks, data breaches, and digital threats
The security of financial assets in bank accounts
The protection of employees from workplace hazards

questionText: Which of the following is a PRIMARY cybersecurity threat to supply chain information systems?
options: Excessive data storage capacity
Ransomware attacks that encrypt supply chain data and demand payment for restoration, disrupting operations
Upgrading supply chain software to a newer version
Employees using approved enterprise software

questionText: "Data encryption" in supply chain e-security refers to:
options: Physically locking data storage devices in a safe
Converting data into a coded format that can only be read by authorized parties with the correct decryption key, protecting sensitive supply chain information from unauthorized access
Deleting sensitive data after it is no longer needed
Restricting access to data by keeping it in printed form only

questionText: A "phishing attack" targeting a supply chain company's procurement team would MOST likely involve:
options: Unauthorized physical entry into the warehouse
Fraudulent emails impersonating trusted suppliers or partners to trick employees into revealing login credentials, authorizing fraudulent payments, or downloading malicious software
Intercepting physical mail sent between suppliers
Hacking into the company's telephone system

questionText: Which of the following BEST describes "multi-factor authentication (MFA)" as an e-security measure?
options: Using multiple passwords for the same account
Requiring users to verify their identity through two or more independent factors (e.g., a password plus a one-time code sent to a mobile device) before accessing a system
Allowing multiple users to share a single login credential
Changing passwords at least three times per year

questionText: In supply chain e-commerce, "supply chain cyber risk" includes which of the following?
options: Only risks related to physical theft of goods in transit
Risks including data breaches of supplier systems, malware in shared supply chain platforms, compromised EDI transactions, and cyberattacks on logistics and payment systems
Only risks associated with employee fraud
Only risks related to e-commerce website downtime

questionText: A company discovers that a hacker has intercepted and altered purchase orders transmitted electronically to suppliers. This type of attack is known as:
options: Denial of Service (DoS) attack
Man-in-the-middle attack, where an attacker intercepts and potentially alters communications between two parties
SQL injection attack on the database
Social engineering attack on employees

questionText: "SSL/TLS certificates" used in e-commerce websites primarily provide:
options: A digital badge showing that the website is popular
Encryption of data transmitted between a user's browser and the web server, ensuring that sensitive information such as payment data is protected from interception
A guarantee that all products sold on the website are authentic
A verification that the company has paid its taxes

questionText: Which of the following is the MOST effective organizational measure to prevent cybersecurity breaches in supply chain systems?
options: Purchasing the most expensive cybersecurity software available
Implementing a comprehensive cybersecurity program including regular employee training, access controls, system audits, patch management, and incident response planning
Limiting all supply chain operations to offline systems
